cells.tense: The pattern is being read while the feeling is still here.
cells.act: gather the feelings that might be felt and look at them
cells.ask: Take what you're ready to put down and list every feeling it might carry — relief, grief, quiet — before choosing anything.
cells.core:
What you recognize about a thing comes through clean right now, and you can put down what's finished without making it a loss. The pattern is read while the feeling is close by, which is why the open hand stays open. The door is right there and your hand is already on it.

The pull of what might be felt is the next thing wanting space. Before you put down what's over, lay out what it could feel like — relief, grief, quiet, all of it — and look at them together, without choosing. Feelings that go unnamed get carried; the ones you can see can go with the thing itself. Nothing needs deciding today.
cells.sheetLine: You can see the pattern and still put it down clean.
cells.verb: reading the pattern before the feeling arrives
cells.place: standing at the door you are meant to open by letting go

cells.tense: The end is being decided before the feeling has had its say.
cells.act: let the structure act instead of announcing it
cells.ask: Settle the ending you've been holding over. Finish it today and tell no one first; the act can speak for itself.
cells.core:
You have already read how it ends, and you are bracing for the release before the thing itself has finished. The call is made, the ending is scheduled, and the feeling that might have come with it gets no time to arrive. People on the other side of this are at a door you have already closed. What is missing isn't decisiveness — it's letting anything land.

Command's own move fits here: let the structure act instead of announcing it. Settle the ending you have been holding over and finish it today. Make no announcement, no case. When the end is small and done, the feeling finds its way in behind it. That is the order this wants — the act done before the explaining begins.
cells.sheetLine: You're ending the thing before the feeling lands.

cells.tense: Something finished, and the grip has not opened since.
cells.act: walk toward what connects, leaving what does not
cells.ask: Choose a connection that still lives and take one real step toward it — a message, a visit. Let a smaller habit fall away behind you.
cells.core:
You are at a door that shut some time back, and your hand is still on the frame. The mind keeps reading a pattern from that finished thing, turning it over as if it were still live, and the hand has not opened. What's over is not being released; it's being rehearsed. The rehearsal takes hours something living could use.

Passage moves by walking, not by pushing feeling into a starved place. Choose one person or one shared thing that still connects, and take one real step toward it — a message, a visit, showing up where it lives. Let a smaller habit fall away behind you as you go. Releasing doesn't have to be arranged. It happens in the walking.

cells.tense: A release is already moving, and the hand doing it hasn't signed.
cells.act: hold the cloud of possible feeling without picking yet
cells.ask: Name every feeling you could have about something you've half-decided, and sit with the whole set for a day without choosing any of them.
cells.core:
Something is being set down in you by your own hand, quietly, with no decision on the record. You would say nothing is happening. The pattern has been read and the setting down is already moving, and the hand doing it hasn't claimed it. Underneath is simpler than the analysis: a pull toward something, felt before it was chosen.

Let the whole cloud of feeling sit. Something in you has half-decided without you — so name the feelings it might hold, all of them, and stay a day without picking. Just see what's there. The choice can come later. Authorship returns the same way it left: a step taken, and the recognition that it was yours.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that patterns still arriving from what has ended are being analyzed on purpose; the record shows recognition at work, not deliberate rumination, so a reader could say this is just thinking, nothing hidden. The ask survives being wrong — looking at a drawn feeling without deciding anything is useful whether or not the pattern belongs to an ending. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is the one that explains what the noticing is for before the noticing has happened; I've cut it. I've also kept the Too Much and Too Little cores apart: one is an end decided before the feeling has spoken, the other is a grip held after the end already happened.
